title: Scripts, Stylesheets, and Resource Hints
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of scripts, stylesheets, and resource hints in a browser document.
Apply at least one relevant rule from this lesson to a small HTML example.
Check the result using browser inspection, a validator, or an accessibility checklist.

content.intro: This lesson turns “Scripts, Stylesheets, and Resource Hints” into a practical authoring skill. You will work with the effect of script placement, understand the choices that matter, and check the result instead of relying on guesswork.
content.why_it_matters: Professional pages need to load efficiently, validate cleanly, adapt to different contexts, and remain understandable to other developers.

content_blocks.title: Resource-loading decisions
content_blocks.alt_text: Avoid lazy-loading the likely largest contentful image, and do not mark every image high priority.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The effect of script placement is one of the decisions covered by Scripts, Stylesheets, and Resource Hints. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: async versus defer
items.text: The defer attribute: runs an external classic script after parsing and preserves document-order execution among deferred scripts.

items.title: Stylesheet loading behavior
items.text: The loading attribute: the requested loading strategy; lazy-load off-screen media, not the primary image needed immediately.

items.title: Preload and resource-priority concepts
items.text: Choose resource hints and loading behavior from measurement, not habit. Preserve intrinsic dimensions, avoid lazy-loading content needed immediately, and prioritize only genuinely important resources.

items.title: Avoiding unnecessary external dependencies
items.text: Avoiding unnecessary external dependencies is one of the decisions covered by Scripts, Stylesheets, and Resource Hints. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: Testing performance instead of guessing
items.text: Form controls need meaningful labels and names, clear instructions, and constraints that match the data. Treat browser validation as feedback for users, not proof that submitted data is trustworthy.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet in an .html file and open it in a modern browser. Inspect the result, then run an HTML validator if the lesson concerns syntax or structure. Example paths are illustrative; provide the referenced files or adjust paths before evaluating media/resource behavior.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Prefer the native semantic element that communicates intent. Do not choose markup solely for its default visual style.

content.task: Create a small HTML example that demonstrates scripts, stylesheets, and resource hints. Keep the markup minimal, give every element a clear purpose, and inspect the rendered result.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the relevant concept from Scripts, Stylesheets, and Resource Hints.
Keep IDs unique and use valid nesting.
Check the result in a browser and record one finding.
hints: Start with the smallest valid example for scripts, stylesheets, and resource hints.
Add one element or attribute at a time, then check the result.
Compare the source and rendered DOM if the behavior surprises you.
content.expected_output: The first image is marked important for early display; the off-screen detail image can load lazily. Use priority hints sparingly.

troubleshooting.symptom: The expected content does not appear.
troubleshooting.check: Confirm the file was saved with an .html extension and inspect its path and nesting.
Check the resolved URL and confirm the referenced file or external resource exists and allows the request.

troubleshooting.symptom: The page looks correct but the markup may be invalid.
troubleshooting.check: Run the Nu Html Checker and follow its first relevant diagnostic, then validate again.

common_mistakes.why: The default appearance is not the element’s main meaning and can make navigation or maintenance harder.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose the element that matches the content purpose, then use CSS for presentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a browser’s recovery means the source is valid
common_mistakes.why: Browsers often recover from malformed markup, which can hide defects and produce unexpected document structure.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the rendered DOM and run a validator against the original source.

common_mistakes.why: Missing files, narrow viewports, keyboard access, invalid input, or other states can expose defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected state plus one realistic edge case and an accessibility path.

summary: Scripts, Stylesheets, and Resource Hints is about expressing document structure or behavior intentionally.
Form controls need meaningful labels and names, clear instructions, and constraints that match the data. Treat browser validation as feedback for users, not proof that submitted data is trustworthy.
Verify both markup and behavior; do not infer correctness from appearance alone.
